title: GLUMETZA (metformin hydrochloride) extended-release tablets: full prescribing information
journal: US Food and Drug Administration, Drugs@FDA, NDA 021748 supplement 31, label revised August 2026
result: Label revised 08/2026; Recent Major Changes list the Boxed Warning and Warnings and Precautions 5.1 (Lactic Acidosis). The approval letter of 11 August 2026 states that FDA notified the applicant on 31 March 2026, under section 505(o)(4) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, of new safety information that should be included in the labeling of metformin-containing products, concerning the risk of lactic acidosis in patients with mitochondrial diseases such as mitochondrial encephalopathy with lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes (MELAS) syndrome and maternally inherited diabetes and deafness (MIDD) who were taking metformin products. Boxed warning: postmarketing cases of metformin-associated lactic acidosis have resulted in death, hypothermia, hypotension and resistant bradyarrhythmias, with blood lactate above 5 mmol/L, anion gap acidosis without ketonuria or ketonaemia, raised lactate to pyruvate ratio and plasma metformin generally above 5 mcg/mL; risk factors are renal impairment, concomitant use of certain drugs such as carbonic anhydrase inhibitors, age 65 years or greater, radiological studies with contrast, surgery and other procedures, hypoxic states such as acute congestive heart failure, excessive alcohol intake, hepatic impairment and mitochondrial diseases. Section 5.1 adds: metformin may increase the risk of lactic acidosis in patients with mitochondrial diseases such as MELAS and MIDD and is not recommended in them; if a patient develops elevated lactic acid levels, with or without neurologic signs and symptoms, discontinue the drug and consider evaluating the patient for MELAS, MIDD or other mitochondrial disease. Section 5.2: in 29-week trials of metformin tablets a decrease to subnormal levels of previously normal serum vitamin B12 occurred in about 7% of patients, possibly through interference with B12 absorption from the B12-intrinsic factor complex, may be associated with anaemia, appears rapidly reversible on discontinuation or supplementation; measure haematologic parameters annually and vitamin B12 every 2 to 3 years. Section 5.3: increased risk of hypoglycaemia with insulin or an insulin secretagogue. Section 5.4: there have been no clinical studies establishing conclusive evidence of macrovascular risk reduction. Section 6.1, add-on to glyburide: hypoglycaemia in 14% of 431 patients on GLUMETZA plus glyburide against 5% of 144 on placebo plus glyburide, diarrhoea 13% against 6%, nausea 7% against 4%; diarrhoea caused discontinuation in 0.7% against none. Section 6.2 postmarketing: cholestatic, hepatocellular and mixed hepatocellular liver injury.
